tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# Backlog: where we lose score, and what to work on

As of 10 October 2026, 21:30. Source: the `tactical` run over the 10 hosted practice cases
(`20261010-211824-practice-tactical`, commit `96f7545`, mean 0.695), its trace and events, and the practice
leaderboard read at 21:35 (we are 5th of 22 with 73.2 points over our best scores; the leader has 79.0).

Every figure below is from that run unless a source is named. The "why" of each problem is read from the trace and
the `thread_hold` events; the rule in `tactical.py` behind each stop has not been traced line by line.

## 1. The cases by lever, with what the run lost

| Lever | Case | Score | EUR above C_best | Rounds used of 10 | How the thread ended |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Price increase | P01 | 0.856 | 8,192 | 2 | held: "their offer meets our ask", supplier still `open` |
| Price increase (copper) | P02 | 0.686 | 14,854 | 2 | supplier `agreed` to our sheet |
| Raw-material surcharge | P08 | 0.570 | 75,422 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Raw-material surcharge | P18 | 0.419 | 42,133 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 5.00 → 5.25 → 5.50, its price |
| Renewal | P03 | 0.905 | 31,992 | 4 | held: "the supplier stopped moving" |
| Renewal | P04 | 0.860 | 324 | 3 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| RFQ | P05 | 0.742 | 21,153 | 3 | supplier `agreed`: we went 30.46 → 28.00 against its 28.79 |
| Bundling | P07 | 0.721 | 25,607 | 4 | held: "last word: take it" on a `final_offer` |
| Capacity | P10 | 0.647 | 212,881 | 2 | `final_offer` in its first reply (33.80, alternative 31.90); we took the alternative |
| Quality | P11 | 0.545 | 43,244 | 4 | held: "last word: take it", supplier still `open` |

### The best any team reached, per case

From the arena's live page (screenshot of 10 October, about 21:05; 24 teams) against our best score per case
(`runs.md`, after P-14):

| Case | Lever | Best team | House agent | Teams that beat the house | Our best | Gap to the best |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P08 | raw-material surcharge | 0.91 | 0.75 | 1 | 0.603 | 0.31 |
| P18 | raw-material surcharge | 0.68 | 0.39 | 17 | 0.467 | 0.21 |

The two raw-material cases hold 0.52 of the 1.16 between us and the best team on every case; P08 at 0.91 was reached
by one team. The practice board showed us 6th with a mean of 0.73; the leader had 0.81.

## 2. The problems, largest first

### 2.1 We stop after two to four of ten rounds

No thread used more than four rounds. In P18 and P05 the supplier agreed to our own rising offer (P18: 5.00 → 5.25
→ 5.50 against its 5.60); in P01 and P11 the thread was held while the supplier's status was still `open`.

- P18: deal 264,784, our upper bound 259,433, C_best 222,651.
- P10 is a different case: the supplier called its first reply final (33.80, with an alternative at 31.90) and we
  took the alternative. The deal costs 1,541,808 against our upper bound of 1,374,881 and C_best 1,328,927; what
  would have moved it is not in the trace.
- P02 closed in round 2 below our own ask (358.45 against 361.34), after we offered an index clause.

### 2.2 Our estimate of what is reachable is too high in leverage cases

The upper bound (`plan` event) against the arena's C_best:

| Case | Upper bound | C_best | Upper bound above C_best |
|---|---|---|---|
| P05 | 272,392 | 223,424 | 21.9 % |
| P18 | 259,433 | 222,651 | 16.5 % |
| P08 | 1,028,315 | 960,309 | 7.1 % |
| P07 | 319,069 | 299,241 | 6.6 % |
| P03 | 4,102,637 | 3,909,043 | 5.0 % |
| P01 | 1,143,596 | 1,096,816 | 4.3 % |
| P10 | 1,374,881 | 1,328,927 | 3.5 % |
| P04 | 197,524 | 196,529 | 0.5 % |
| P02 | 2,282,867 | 2,235,514 | 2.1 % |
| P11 | 710,733 | 722,500 | -1.6 % |

An offer inside a bound that is too high counts as good enough, so the thread closes early (2.1).

### 2.3 A lever the supplier names is not pulled

P11: the supplier wrote "Faster payment would help us more than anything" in four replies, and "If you want a lower
price, we need to drop the chargebacks". The profile had it as `cash_short`. Its price went 47.00 → 48.50 → 47.00 →
46.50 → 46.50 and we took it with six rounds left. P07: "A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the
price" in round 4.

### 2.4 Arguments that are spent for nothing

- The price-history argument came back "it holds, but it does not change our calculation" in five cases (P18, P08,
  P10, P02, P11). It takes one of the three argument slots of the first e-mail each time.
- P07: the forecast was cited in four e-mails; three came back `duplicate`, and the supplier answered "that volume
  change was already factored into our previous calculation" three times.

### 2.5 What is no longer a problem: the volume question

On 10 October in the afternoon the most common supplier sentence was "Which volume can you commit to?", unanswered
(`rejections.md`, row 1). In this run the forecast argument came back "it holds and we took it into account" in P18,
P08, P02, P07 and P11.

### 2.6 A final offer is final on practice

`playbook`'s closing offer after a final offer made three suppliers walk away (P04, P07, P18):
[`benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md`](benchmarks/2026-10-10-playbook-none.md). Problem 2.1 is about the rounds
before a final offer, not about pushing past one.

### 2.7 Our cost of a deal misses the relationship charge

One row per idea, newest at the bottom of each table. The rule is in [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#ideas-tried). A row
says what was tried, where it was measured, the result, and why it worked or failed - or "unknown" when no run has
settled it. Figures are from the run named in the row ([`runs.md`](runs.md), [`benchmarks/`](benchmarks/)).

Result: **worked** (kept), **failed** (dropped), **mixed**, **unknown** (not yet measured or not separable).

## Mechanics of the offer

# Competition facts beyond the brief

As of 10 October 2026. Source: the arena's FAQ page (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, "Questions from the room"), pasted
into the session that evening, read against the brief (`negotiation-arena-kit/brief/brief.md`). Only what the brief
does not say, or says differently, is listed; the brief stays the reference for everything else.

## Scoring

- **C_open is the cheapest opening quote that keeps our must-haves.** The brief says "the best opening quote".
- **A deal worse than the opening scores 0**, as does a broken must-have. No deal scores the alternative, 0 without
  one.
- **Every case weighs the same.** The score ranks, not the euros saved; "€ saved" on the board is a side number.
- **Final:** wave score = the mean of the wave's case scores × 100; points = the sum of five waves, up to 500. A
  case still open at the 8-minute cap, **or never opened**, counts as no deal. Ties: more deals, then fewer rounds.

## Practice

- **Practice does not rank.** The best score per hosted case counts, and the practice board shows the mean over the
  10 hosted cases; the FAQ calls it "for learning".
- **Quota:** the FAQ and the brief say 200 sessions a day. `negotiator me` showed a limit of 650 for our key on
  10 October (reset 2026-10-11 12:47 UTC). Read the balance, not the FAQ.
- **Old replays:** `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice`, then `/replay/<session_id>`.
- **One run gives C_open and C_best of a case;** after that `arena_kit.total_cost` scores any term sheet offline.

## Running the final

- **Nothing is deployed and Tacto does not run our code.** We submit the repo and the commit hash on ehl.gg and run
  that commit ourselves; the agent polls from before 12:00 until the last wave has closed.
- **The FAQ advises a cloud VM over a laptop on the venue Wi-Fi** (sleep, dropped connections).
- `arena-sim serve --no-clock` runs the kit's scripted supplier without the 60-second clock.

## The FAQ's worked example: P01, score 0.76

The page replays one negotiation on P01 (C_open 1,153,780, C_best 1,096,816) that ends at EUR 134.50, 30 days, valid
from 1 January 2027. What the buyer did, in order:

1. Opened with the relationship ("you held your prices for a quarter in 2022"), one falling index with its ID and
   figure (`idx:PPI-D351@2026-08`, −3.7 %), an offer to pay faster, and two sheets (129.90 at 60 days, 128.90 at 30
   days), both from January. The supplier: "We did not know that - a fair point", and moved the date to January.
2. Asked "Can you meet us at 131.50?" with two sheets. The supplier: "Which figures is that based on? Please send us
   the data."
3. Answered with the should-cost estimate and its ID (`cost:310010`, EUR 132.64 before margin) and "we want you to
   earn a fair margin on top". The supplier verified it and proposed 134.50.

**The FAQ's own comparison:** the same index sent as an ultimatum ("unacceptable … or we go elsewhere") got 136.50

# Competition facts beyond the brief

As of 10 October 2026. Source: the arena's FAQ page (`https://arena.tacto.ai`, "Questions from the room"), pasted
into the session that evening, read against the brief (`negotiation-arena-kit/brief/brief.md`). Only what the brief
does not say, or says differently, is listed; the brief stays the reference for everything else.

## Scoring

- **C_open is the cheapest opening quote that keeps our must-haves.** The brief says "the best opening quote".
- **A deal worse than the opening scores 0**, as does a broken must-have. No deal scores the alternative, 0 without
  one.
- **Every case weighs the same.** The score ranks, not the euros saved; "€ saved" on the board is a side number.
- **Final:** wave score = the mean of the wave's case scores × 100; points = the sum of five waves, up to 500. A
  case still open at the 8-minute cap, **or never opened**, counts as no deal. Ties: more deals, then fewer rounds.

## Practice

- **Practice does not rank.** The best score per hosted case counts, and the practice board shows the mean over the
  10 hosted cases; the FAQ calls it "for learning".
- **Quota:** the FAQ and the brief say 200 sessions a day. `negotiator me` showed a limit of 650 for our key on
  10 October (reset 2026-10-11 12:47 UTC). Read the balance, not the FAQ.
- **Old replays:** `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice`, then `/replay/<session_id>`.
- **One run gives C_open and C_best of a case;** after that `arena_kit.total_cost` scores any term sheet offline.

## Running the final

- **Nothing is deployed and Tacto does not run our code.** We submit the repo and the commit hash on ehl.gg and run
  that commit ourselves; the agent polls from before 12:00 until the last wave has closed.
- **The FAQ advises a cloud VM over a laptop on the venue Wi-Fi** (sleep, dropped connections).
- `arena-sim serve --no-clock` runs the kit's scripted supplier without the 60-second clock.

# What moves the arena's suppliers: our 293 practice sessions

As of 11 October 2026, about 01:30. Source: every ended practice session of our team key (293; P01-P18, all
strategies and commits since 10 October). They come from `negotiator session <sid>` (trace, claim checks, scores) and
`negotiator backoffice <sid>` (the supplier's internal notes after the case). Both are read-only calls that spend no
quota. The raw files sit in `agent/data/replays/` and `agent/data/backoffice/` (git-ignored). The analysis scripts
were one-off and are not in the repository.

These are correlations across our own sessions, so strategy versions are mixed. Where the back office states the
supplier's rule outright, that rule is direct evidence; everything else is a lead to test with one practice session
per case.

## 1. The supplier's rules, from its back office

| Note in the back office | Count | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| "The buyer shows a much lower rival quote. I give half the step now and check the rest." | 50 | P05 |
| "Checked: give the rest of the step." (the next round) | 47 | P05 |
| "The buyer wants more than my band allows (band ends at …, buyer at …). Approve a further step?" | 10 | P02, P03, P10 |
| "Approved: you may go further, within our rules." | 7 | P02, P03 |
| "My call: hold." | 135 | all but P10 |
| "My call: walk_away." | 7 | P01, P04, P05, P18 |

- **RFQ (P05).** A much lower rival quote buys a step in two halves: half now, the rest after the check, in the next
  reply, whatever we send.
  - Best P05 session (0.839, `2d73b8dc2cadc8c6`): we cited the rival's 31.5. Dralveck went 36 → 29.5, we asked 27.85
    and it agreed at 27.85 (the rest of the step).
  - A 0.742 session (`0a55ee9e09cf56d9`): same opening, Dralveck went 36 → 30.5. We then offered 28.79 on our own and
    it agreed at once, before it would have given the rest anyway.
- **Approval ladder (P02, P03, P10).** An ask beyond the manager's band goes to a committee, which approved a further
  step in 7 of the 10 cases we saw. We reached the band only 10 times in 293 sessions.

## 2. What the supplier says about our data

The most common sentences (numbers masked):

| Sentence | Count |
|---|---|
| "We checked the price history data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 184 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 104 |
| "Which figures is that based on? Please send us the data." | 90 |
| "We checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 80 |
| "We checked the rival quote data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 79 |
| "We see your figures, but we cannot give up margin right now. Faster payment would help us more than anything." | 54 |
| "We checked the quality record data you cited; it holds and we took it into account." | 48 |
| "We checked the volume change data you cited; it holds, but it does not change our calculation." | 40 |

Claim results: 905 verified, 35 duplicate, 4 contradicted.

### A duplicate is a series, not an ID

`api.md` says each ID counts once per case. On P08 (`../runs.md` P-33) a second fall of PPI-C2431 over a window
with IDs we had not cited (05 → 07, after 06 → 08 in round 1) came back `duplicate`: "it holds, but this kind of
fact was already taken into account in our previous calculation". One argument per index series per case.

### P08: what sets the price (31 sessions)

The supplier makes one big step in its first reply, then small ones, and calls its offer final in round 3. Its final
offer sat 0.04-0.18 under its first reply. The first reply depends on our first message:

| Our first message | Its first reply |
|---|---|
| PPI-C2431's fall + AS-14404's fall + order history | 5.41 (13 sessions) |
| order history + forecast, no PPI | 5.46 |
| AS-14404 alone, or with LCI-C | 5.57 |
| a delivery-record complaint (+ forecast) | 5.71 and 6.10 |

AS-14404 is answered "not our reality: covered at fixed prices until March 2027"; PPI-C2431 (36 % of its cost by our
cost drivers) is "taken into account"; a complaint raises the price. From round 3 we had nothing left to cite in
every session.

## 3. Our step against the supplier's next reply

Rounds 2 and later; "our step" is the change of our lowest ask against our previous ask to the same supplier.

| Our step | Replies | Supplier's mean drop | It held its price | Final offer | Agreed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no move | 65 | 0.60 % | 32 % | 25 % | 18 % |
| under 1 % | 245 | 0.59 % | 34 % | 31 % | 4 % |
| 1-3 % | 126 | 1.75 % | 12 % | 34 % | 13 % |
| over 3 % | 209 | 1.86 % | 12 % | 16 % | 34 % |

Steps under 1 % get a held price a third of the time; steps over 3 % get "agreed" a third of the time, which is the
supplier taking our concession.

## 4. The first message

The supplier's price drop in its first reply, compared within the same case and supplier (paired; the number of
suppliers where the difference is positive in brackets):

| First message | Difference in the first reply's drop |
|---|---|
| 2 or more cited arguments | +1.71 pp (8 of 12) |
| no cited argument | −2.52 pp (1 of 5) |
| first ask 15 % or more under the quote | +3.60 pp (5 of 9) |
| first ask under 8 % below the quote | −3.72 pp (4 of 9) |
| 2 or more questions | −2.39 pp (3 of 12) |
| a single term sheet | −2.24 pp (1 of 8) |
| a quality record cited | −2.18 pp (0 of 4) |
| a delivery record cited | −1.65 pp (4 of 12) |
| price history cited | +2.14 pp (6 of 8) |

Within each case, the session's score ranks with the first reply's drop at Spearman +0.63 (positive in 10 of 10
cases). It also ranks with the number of cited arguments (+0.55, 10 of 10), with "took it into account" replies (+0.47,
10 of 10) and with questions asked (−0.10; top third 0.6 questions per session, bottom third 2.2).

## 5. P08: the index clause

Offline with `arena_kit.total_cost` on the deal of `20261011-004458-practice-tactical` (P08, price 5.42, payment 90
days, 24 months):

| Index clause | C |
|---|---|
| none | 1,020,781 |
| deadband 5 % | 1,030,030 |
| deadband 3 % (the deal) | 1,039,278 |
| deadband 0 % | 1,053,152 |

The case expects AS-14404 to rise 6 % a year, so the clause we gave cost 18,497 against none: 0.105 of the score. The
supplier's final offer also held a 5 % deadband sheet at 5.46 (C 1,037,614), cheaper for us than the one we accepted.

## 6. Leads to test (one practice session per case each)

1. Steps of 1-3 % of C instead of 0.4 % crumbs, under 3 % so the supplier does not simply agree.
2. RFQ: cite a much lower rival offer to each bidder, then do not raise our ask in the next round - the rest of its
   step comes after its check. Cite a rival's new lower offer as soon as it appears (each offer has its own ID).
3. Raw material with a rising index: price the index clause in C and do not give it where it costs more than its
   price difference; offer payment or contract length instead.
4. First message: two or three verified arguments, no quality or delivery complaint outside quality cases, at most one
   question, a menu of options, a first ask at least 15 % under the quote outside strategic cases.
5. Approval-ladder cases: one ask beyond the supplier's band, so the committee is asked for a further step.
# Investigation, 10 October 2026: scoring, payment terms, relationship charge, term menu

No arena session was played for this. Everything is read from local files or computed offline.

**Data read** (other agents were adding runs while this was written; the snapshot is fixed by the newest run named):

- 64 practice sessions in 8 run directories under `agent/runs/*practice*` (61 deals, 3 no-deals), up to
  `20261010-234407-practice-tactical` with its first 2 sessions (P01, P02);
- 89 sandbox sessions under `agent/runs/*sandbox*` (46 on D01, 43 on D02), all deals;
- `negotiation-arena-kit/brief/brief.md`, `brief/api.md`, `starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py`, `data/world.sqlite`.

**Source labels used below:**

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [docs] | `brief.md` or `api.md` |
| [code] | `arena_kit/cost.py`, the published cost function |
| [practice] | a recorded practice session; cited as `run/session`, run names without the `20261010-` prefix |
| [sandbox] | a recorded sandbox session |
| [computed] | the published cost function applied to a stated term sheet, with the supplier fitted in section 3 |
| [inference] | our reading; not established |

"Score points" always means EUR divided by `c_open − c_best` of that case.

## 1. Scoring

### 1.1 How C is built

[docs] `api.md`, "Cost and score"; [code] `cost_breakdown`. Both say the same:

```
years     = min(contract_months / 12, horizon_years)        a single order counts as 1 year
committed = volume_per_year · years
covered   = min(volume_per_year, need_per_year) · years
pre       = units between the horizon start and effective_date, at current_unit_price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + (committed − pre) · unit_price
uncovered = (need_per_year · horizon_years − covered) · fallback_unit_price

C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)
  + spend · interest_rate · (reference_payment_days − payment_days) / 360
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new_spend · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband/100) · sign(index_path)     index clause only
  + new_spend · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                       index clause only
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years  stabilise, secure_supply
```

Answers to the questions asked:

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plain sum or discounted? | Plain sum. A unit bought in year 2 counts the same as one bought in year 1. There is no discount factor anywhere in the function. | [code] |
| Is an interest rate modelled? | Only in the payment term: `spend × interest_rate × (reference_payment_days − payment_days) / 360`. Simple interest, 360-day year, linear in days. Paying later than the reference earns the same rate (the term turns negative). | [code], [docs] |
| Which rate and reference? | `interest_rate` 0.08 and `reference_payment_days` 60 in all 10 practice cases and both sandbox cases. | [practice], [sandbox] case files |
| Is inflation modelled? | No. A fixed price stays fixed for the whole horizon at no cost. The only price path is `index_paths`, and it counts only if the deal carries an index clause (P02 copper +5 %, P08 and P18 alloy surcharge +6 %). | [code], case files |
| Does a contract longer than the horizon count? | No. 36 months gives the same C as 24 months when the horizon is 2 years. | [code] `_years`; [computed] section 4 |
| Does volume above the need count? | Yes, in full: committed units are bought "needed or not". | [code] |

### 1.2 From C to the score

[docs], [code] `score`:

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

| Outcome | Score | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `C_deal ≥ C_open` | 0 | [code]; [practice] P02 `221425-practice-tactical-slow25/e5471e792b2e64a9` |
| `C_deal ≤ C_best` | 1 | [code] |
| a broken must-have | 0 | [docs] |
| no deal, case has an alternative | the alternative's score | [docs]; [practice] P07 `212101-practice-playbook/6bcba80947d374a4`: 0.121 with `c_alt` 379,916 |
| no deal, alternative dearer than C_open, or none | 0 | [practice] P04 `212101-practice-playbook/3bf0807b2eebd8b1` (`c_alt` 203,169 > `c_open` 198,846) |

What the two yardsticks are, as far as the records show:

- **C_open** is the opening sheet filled with the supplier's standard terms. Recomputed with the kit it matches the

**Source labels used below:**

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| [docs] | `brief.md` or `api.md` |
| [code] | `arena_kit/cost.py`, the published cost function |
| [practice] | a recorded practice session; cited as `run/session`, run names without the `20261010-` prefix |

"Score points" always means EUR divided by `c_open − c_best` of that case.

## 1. Scoring

### 1.1 How C is built

[docs] `api.md`, "Cost and score"; [code] `cost_breakdown`. Both say the same:

```
years     = min(contract_months / 12, horizon_years)        a single order counts as 1 year
committed = volume_per_year · years
covered   = min(volume_per_year, need_per_year) · years
pre       = units between the horizon start and effective_date, at current_unit_price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + (committed − pre) · unit_price
uncovered = (need_per_year · horizon_years − covered) · fallback_unit_price

C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)
  + spend · interest_rate · (reference_payment_days − payment_days) / 360
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new_spend · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband/100) · sign(index_path)     index clause only
  + new_spend · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                       index clause only
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years  stabilise, secure_supply
```

Answers to the questions asked:

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Plain sum or discounted? | Plain sum. A unit bought in year 2 counts the same as one bought in year 1. There is no discount factor anywhere in the function. | [code] |
| Is an interest rate modelled? | Only in the payment term: `spend × interest_rate × (reference_payment_days − payment_days) / 360`. Simple interest, 360-day year, linear in days. Paying later than the reference earns the same rate (the term turns negative). | [code], [docs] |
| Which rate and reference? | `interest_rate` 0.08 and `reference_payment_days` 60 in all 10 practice cases and both sandbox cases. | [practice], [sandbox] case files |
| Is inflation modelled? | No. A fixed price stays fixed for the whole horizon at no cost. The only price path is `index_paths`, and it counts only if the deal carries an index clause (P02 copper +5 %, P08 and P18 alloy surcharge +6 %). | [code], case files |
| Does a contract longer than the horizon count? | No. 36 months gives the same C as 24 months when the horizon is 2 years. | [code] `_years`; [computed] section 4 |
| Does volume above the need count? | Yes, in full: committed units are bought "needed or not". | [code] |

### 1.2 From C to the score

[docs], [code] `score`:

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

| Outcome | Score | Source |

| `C_deal ≥ C_open` | 0 | [code]; [practice] P02 `221425-practice-tactical-slow25/e5471e792b2e64a9` |
| `C_deal ≤ C_best` | 1 | [code] |
| a broken must-have | 0 | [docs] |
| no deal, case has an alternative | the alternative's score | [docs]; [practice] P07 `212101-practice-playbook/6bcba80947d374a4`: 0.121 with `c_alt` 379,916 |
| no deal, alternative dearer than C_open, or none | 0 | [practice] P04 `212101-practice-playbook/3bf0807b2eebd8b1` (`c_alt` 203,169 > `c_open` 198,846) |

# Agent strategies: logic and results

As of 10 October 2026, commit `8670be2`.

**Case score:** a number from 0 to 1, `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. It is the share of the possible saving
we got, measured from the best opening offer.

**Where we played:** every run was on the arena's sandbox, cases D01 and D02, against real supplier bots. No practice
quota (200 sessions per day) was spent.

**The simulator is e2e testing, not a metric:**
- Runs on the local `arena-sim` check only the mechanics: client, runner, message format, closing a case.
- The result there is pass/fail. Its scripted supplier concedes a fixed 2 % per round, so its score is not used to
  compare strategies.
- Every strategy passes e2e: 3 of 3 deals, arguments `verified`.

## Strategies

| Strategy | Code | Author | LLM | Logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **baseline v1** (replaced) | `strategy/baseline.py` before `8670be2` | Mikhail Fadin | no | Target = opening price minus an anchor (leverage −10 %, routine −7 %, stabilise −4 %, secure_supply −3 %). Concessions on a fixed schedule: 0 → 30 → 50 → 65 → 78 → 88 → 95 % of the gap. Three term sheets: C-optimal for us, the supplier's price +1 %, shorter payment at equal C. Checkable arguments from the data. A thread is held on `agreed` or `final_offer`, on a stall or in the last round. Close: the cheapest standing offer, if it beats the alternative. |
| **baseline v2** (current) | `strategy/baseline.py` (`8670be2`) | Mikhail Fadin | no | Everything from v1 plus three fixes from the sandbox analysis. **(1) Equal-C menu:** every sheet in a message costs us the same; the sheet on the supplier's own structure is cheaper by exactly how much worse that structure is for us. **(2) Deeper anchors** (leverage −18 %, routine −12 %, stabilise −8 %) **and reciprocal concessions:** our step is at most the supplier's last step (at least 0.4 %), on a slower schedule. **(3) Consistency:** a structure's price never drops between rounds; a thread is held only when the supplier's offer is no worse than ours **in C**. |
| **llm** | `strategy/llm_strategy.py` | Mikhail Fadin | yes (currently `ollama:qwen3.6`) | Runs on top of baseline v2. Before the session opens, the model reads the supplier's dossier (letters, notes, news, history, credit index) and builds a profile. Each round it picks the stance, concession share, trade lever and arguments, and writes the e-mail text. Code builds the term sheets, inserts the checked arguments and strips figures and IDs from the model's text. If the model has not answered within 30 s, baseline makes the move. |
| **tactical** (default) | `strategy/tactical.py`, `profile.py`, `guards.py`, `lessons.py` | DavidtheRavinger | no | **Policy per category goal:** anchor, concession speed, reciprocity. About 12 supplier traits found in the data by regular expressions adjust it: cash-short, approval ladder, idle capacity, hedged and so on. **Concessions in C:** Boulware curve; no move from the supplier, no move from us; three stalls end the thread. **Menu** of three sheets at equal C, including a trade on a lever the supplier values. **Learns within the case:** drops arguments that came back `contradicted` or `irrelevant`, parses the cost breakdown. Probes a `final_offer` once, when the supplier walking away would cost us little. **Guards** before accept and before sending; `lessons.md` after the run. |
| **judged / jev** (planned) | – | – | yes | Tactical at three aggressiveness levels (soft, normal, hard); a judge model picks the move. Waiting for the model. |

## Results: arena sandbox (real bots)

| Strategy | D01: price increase, stabilise | D02: RFQ, 2 suppliers, leverage | Mean | Rounds D01 / D02 | Time D01 / D02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline v1 | 0.268 | 0.425 | 0.346 | 5 / 9 | 91 / 187 s |
| llm (before fixes) | 0.100 | 0.455 | 0.277 | 4 / 7 | 130 / 167 s |
| llm (after fixes, before the equal-C menu) | 0.210 | 0.448 | 0.329 | 6 / 11 | 173 / 274 s |
| **baseline v2** | **0.843** | **0.629** | **0.736** | 3 / 8 | 76 / 162 s |
| llm on v2 | 0.663 | 0.545 | 0.604 | 3 / 8 | 90 / 175 s |
| tactical | 0.773 | 0.505 | 0.639 | 4 / 7 | – |

## Conclusions

1. **The mechanics drove the gain, not the LLM.** The equal-C menu and reciprocal concessions lifted baseline on the
   arena from 0.346 to 0.736. Tactical is built on the same ideas and is also far above the old baseline.
2. **The results are noisy.** One run per case, and the bots answer non-deterministically, so the gap between
   baseline v2 (0.736) and tactical (0.639) is not reliable. It needs repeated runs.
3. **Tactical probably trails on D02 because of its shallow anchor.** Its anchor is at most −15 % below the quote,
   while the supplier's floor there is about −24 % below the opening.
4. **The LLM layer does not pay off yet.** On v2 it is worse than plain baseline: the model concedes more cautiously
   than these bots require. The natural place for a model is choosing the aggressiveness (jev), not replacing the logic.
5. **The test base is narrow.** Everything was measured on two demo cases. The real practice cases with supplier data
   (P01–P19) are untested.

## What we learned about the supplier bots (trace and back office)

- **Term structure can matter more than price.** In D01 the best deal is a 24-month contract, 60 days' payment and a
  price valid from April, at about €50.13 per unit. With a 12-month contract the second year of the horizon is bought at
  the fallback price: roughly €30k more at almost the same unit price.
- **A supplier's floor can be far below its opening.** In D02 the best deal is about €13.0 per unit against openings of
  16.0 and 17.1 (−19 to −24 %). An early `agreed` to our offer means we overpaid.
- **The bots name their levers.** Examples: "Faster payment is welcome; we can reflect it in the price", "A binding
  higher volume would help".
- **Citing a cheaper rival works.** Example: "I give half the step now and check the rest".
# Разбор работы команды: вечер 10 октября 2026

Написано 11 октября 2026, около 01:00 UTC. Разобраны 19 коммитов в `main`, от `237335a` до `b3f06da`.

Источники цифр: эти коммиты, `runs.md`, записи бенчмарков и `negotiator me` на момент написания. На `b3f06da` проходит
`make test`: 52 теста, включая `test_llm_strategy.py`.

## Что сделали

### David: код tactical (13 коммитов)

- **Фиксы из ревью tactical:**
  - final offer теперь принимается;
  - у поставщика просим более дешёвые альтернативы;
  - каждый аргумент цитируется один раз;
  - отказанные варианты убираются;
  - верхняя граница пересчитывается после каждого ответа поставщика;
  - вместо семи подогнанных коэффициентов (`FLOOR_FACTOR`) — двухуровневая оценка пола.
- **`belief.py`** — живая оценка пола поставщика, пересчитывается после каждого ответа. Пол хранится как ценность для
  поставщика, а не как цена, поэтому одно число подходит к любой структуре условий. На входе:
  - офферы поставщика;
  - его альтернативы (по разнице в днях оплаты видно, сколько ему стоят деньги);
  - фразы вида «cannot go below X»;
  - экстраполяция его затухающих шагов.

  На выходе — самый дешёвый для нас по C пакет.
- **`ledger.py`** — журнал аргументов, каждый ID используется один раз. Источники:
  - из данных — драйверы затрат, которые недавно упали;
  - драйвер, на который ссылается сам поставщик, — разворачиваем против него, если он упал;
  - хеджирование поставщика и свободная мощность.
- **`conduct.py`** — 10 правил поведения. Guard выкидывает фразы с неизвестными ID и блокирует блеф.
- **RFQ:** соглашение принимаем только после того, как ответили все конкуренты. Стратегических поставщиков бережём.
- **`equal_c`:** все варианты в одном письме стоят нам одинаковый C. P02: 0.167 → 0.731.
- **patient (`b3f06da`):** наша оценка пола больше не закрывает открытые переговоры. Вместо этого просим ещё раз чуть
  ниже открытого оффера поставщика. P01: 0.831 → 0.946, P18: 0.618 → 0.685, P10: 0.663 → 0.601.
- **Флаги `tactical+<flag>`:** включают по одному изменению. Каждый флаг мерили одной сессией на кейс, большинство
  отбросили (`benchmarks/2026-10-10-flags-paired.md`).

### Vector: замеры и документация

# Agent strategies: logic and results

As of 10 October 2026, commit `8670be2`.

**Case score:** a number from 0 to 1, `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. It is the share of the possible saving
we got, measured from the best opening offer.

**Where we played:** every run was on the arena's sandbox, cases D01 and D02, against real supplier bots. No practice
quota (200 sessions per day) was spent.

**The simulator is e2e testing, not a metric:**
- Runs on the local `arena-sim` check only the mechanics: client, runner, message format, closing a case.
- The result there is pass/fail. Its scripted supplier concedes a fixed 2 % per round, so its score is not used to
  compare strategies.
- Every strategy passes e2e: 3 of 3 deals, arguments `verified`.

## Strategies

| Strategy | Code | Author | LLM | Logic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **baseline v1** (replaced) | `strategy/baseline.py` before `8670be2` | Mikhail Fadin | no | Target = opening price minus an anchor (leverage −10 %, routine −7 %, stabilise −4 %, secure_supply −3 %). Concessions on a fixed schedule: 0 → 30 → 50 → 65 → 78 → 88 → 95 % of the gap. Three term sheets: C-optimal for us, the supplier's price +1 %, shorter payment at equal C. Checkable arguments from the data. A thread is held on `agreed` or `final_offer`, on a stall or in the last round. Close: the cheapest standing offer, if it beats the alternative. |
| **baseline v2** (current) | `strategy/baseline.py` (`8670be2`) | Mikhail Fadin | no | Everything from v1 plus three fixes from the sandbox analysis. **(1) Equal-C menu:** every sheet in a message costs us the same; the sheet on the supplier's own structure is cheaper by exactly how much worse that structure is for us. **(2) Deeper anchors** (leverage −18 %, routine −12 %, stabilise −8 %) **and reciprocal concessions:** our step is at most the supplier's last step (at least 0.4 %), on a slower schedule. **(3) Consistency:** a structure's price never drops between rounds; a thread is held only when the supplier's offer is no worse than ours **in C**. |
| **llm** | `strategy/llm_strategy.py` | Mikhail Fadin | yes (currently `ollama:qwen3.6`) | Runs on top of baseline v2. Before the session opens, the model reads the supplier's dossier (letters, notes, news, history, credit index) and builds a profile. Each round it picks the stance, concession share, trade lever and arguments, and writes the e-mail text. Code builds the term sheets, inserts the checked arguments and strips figures and IDs from the model's text. If the model has not answered within 30 s, baseline makes the move. |
| **tactical** (default) | `strategy/tactical.py`, `profile.py`, `guards.py`, `lessons.py` | DavidtheRavinger | no | **Policy per category goal:** anchor, concession speed, reciprocity. About 12 supplier traits found in the data by regular expressions adjust it: cash-short, approval ladder, idle capacity, hedged and so on. **Concessions in C:** Boulware curve; no move from the supplier, no move from us; three stalls end the thread. **Menu** of three sheets at equal C, including a trade on a lever the supplier values. **Learns within the case:** drops arguments that came back `contradicted` or `irrelevant`, parses the cost breakdown. Probes a `final_offer` once, when the supplier walking away would cost us little. **Guards** before accept and before sending; `lessons.md` after the run. |
| **judged / jev** (planned) | – | – | yes | Tactical at three aggressiveness levels (soft, normal, hard); a judge model picks the move. Waiting for the model. |

## Results: arena sandbox (real bots)

| Strategy | D01: price increase, stabilise | D02: RFQ, 2 suppliers, leverage | Mean | Rounds D01 / D02 | Time D01 / D02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline v1 | 0.268 | 0.425 | 0.346 | 5 / 9 | 91 / 187 s |
| llm (before fixes) | 0.100 | 0.455 | 0.277 | 4 / 7 | 130 / 167 s |
| llm (after fixes, before the equal-C menu) | 0.210 | 0.448 | 0.329 | 6 / 11 | 173 / 274 s |
| **baseline v2** | **0.843** | **0.629** | **0.736** | 3 / 8 | 76 / 162 s |
| llm on v2 | 0.663 | 0.545 | 0.604 | 3 / 8 | 90 / 175 s |
| tactical | 0.773 | 0.505 | 0.639 | 4 / 7 | – |

## Conclusions

1. **The mechanics drove the gain, not the LLM.** The equal-C menu and reciprocal concessions lifted baseline on the
   arena from 0.346 to 0.736. Tactical is built on the same ideas and is also far above the old baseline.
2. **The results are noisy.** One run per case, and the bots answer non-deterministically, so the gap between
   baseline v2 (0.736) and tactical (0.639) is not reliable. It needs repeated runs.
3. **Tactical probably trails on D02 because of its shallow anchor.** Its anchor is at most −15 % below the quote,
   while the supplier's floor there is about −24 % below the opening.
4. **The LLM layer does not pay off yet.** On v2 it is worse than plain baseline: the model concedes more cautiously
   than these bots require. The natural place for a model is choosing the aggressiveness (jev), not replacing the logic.
5. **The test base is narrow.** Everything was measured on two demo cases. The real practice cases with supplier data
   (P01–P19) are untested.

## What we learned about the supplier bots (trace and back office)

- **Term structure can matter more than price.** In D01 the best deal is a 24-month contract, 60 days' payment and a
  price valid from April, at about €50.13 per unit. With a 12-month contract the second year of the horizon is bought at
  the fallback price: roughly €30k more at almost the same unit price.
- **A supplier's floor can be far below its opening.** In D02 the best deal is about €13.0 per unit against openings of
  16.0 and 17.1 (−19 to −24 %). An early `agreed` to our offer means we overpaid.
- **The bots name their levers.** Examples: "Faster payment is welcome; we can reflect it in the price", "A binding
  higher volume would help".
- **Citing a cheaper rival works.** Example: "I give half the step now and check the rest".

  - **Merge:** it does not merge cleanly, but both conflicts are trivial. I tried it in a temporary worktree.
    - `agent/src/negotiator/session.py` (the clock reset after a reply): both sides fixed the same bug, "the clock runs from the reply, not from the end of the download". Take the branch's hunk.
    - `agent/docs/runs.md`: both sides added rows S-18/S-19. Keep both and renumber.
  - **Tests:** after the merge (branch hunk kept), `uv run pytest -q` gives 103 passed, 2 skipped, and `ruff check` is clean. I removed my worktree. The checkout and the submodule are unchanged; the other `tmp/wt-*` worktrees are not mine.
  
  ### 2. Is the branch correct?
  The core idea is sound. It adds `Turn` (one arena call per session at a time, the clock that ends first goes first) and reads the arena's state when a clock runs low (`_sync_if_due`, `_sync`). It also:
  - reads timeout answers into the thread (`thread_messages`, `timeout_message`);
  - drops a stale move when `version` moved (a timeout answer arrived while it waited);
  - counts our timeouts against the round limit (`arena_rounds`);
  - falls back to another thread for walk-away after a 422;
  - takes the arena's timeout count in `finalize`.
  
  `Turn` is not reentrant, but no path takes it twice: `_close` → `_refreshed_standing` → `_sync_thread`, and `_send` → `_refresh_after_conflict` → `_sync`, never take it again. Lock order (`_lock` before turn) is consistent, so there is no deadlock.
  
  Findings:
  - **Medium – the close at the deadline can overrun the wave cap** (main has the same problem). In `runner.py` `_negotiate`, after `stop.set()` the `with ThreadPoolExecutor` exit waits for every worker. A worker that already decided still sends: `send` checks only `ended`, not `stop`, including while it waits in `Turn`. With N suppliers, N queued e-mails go one after another (practice replies took 22–46 s, 83 s at most) before `conclude` runs. That can eat the 90 s margin (`CLOSE_BEFORE_DEADLINE_S`), and the case then ends with `wave_cap`, which means no deal.
  - **Medium – a keepalive can block the deadline check.** The coordinator's keepalive (`runner.py` ~L135–145 on the branch, L115–123 on main) has no deadline guard. It blocks the coordinator's loop for its queue wait plus the reply (on the branch up to about 2×60 s), and the deadline check doesn't run meanwhile. Keepalives on held threads also take session turns from live threads, which is exactly what makes clocks run out with 3 suppliers.
  - **Low – a dropped message still marks its arguments as used.** When a move is dropped as stale, `decide` has already changed the plan (`plan.used_sentences`, `used_refs`, `alternatives_taken` in `tactical.py`). Arguments that were never sent count as used.
  - **Low – one slow download holds the whole session.** Documents are now downloaded inside the turn (`_send` → `_with_documents`). This is correct (no queueing at the arena), but a slow download delays every thread of the session.
  - **Low – resync depends on message-id format.** `_round_of` parses `msg:<sup>-<round>-<n>`. If the final arena formats ids differently, it returns None and the forced resync on a skipped round never fires. The 409 path still recovers.
  - **Without timeouts** behaviour is the same apart from:

client: ArenaClient,
    recorder: Recorder,
    new_strategy: StrategyFactory,
    data: WorldData | None = None,
    *,
    waves: int = 5,
    parallel: int = 10,
    poll: float = 3.0,
) -> list[dict]:
    """The Live Final: poll the case list, play every case of each started wave in parallel within its
    cap, until `waves` waves have closed. Reads only our own cases and sessions."""
    if not client.settings.final_mode:
        raise RuntimeError("set NEGOTIATOR_FINAL=1: final mode blocks the live feed for the agent")
    started: dict[str, object] = {}
    closed: set[int] = set()
    caps: dict[int, float] = {}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel, thread_name_prefix="final") as pool:
        while len(closed) < waves or not all(f.done() for f in started.values()):
            try:
                cases = client.cases("final")
            except ArenaError as e:
                if e.status != 403:  # 403: no wave yet
                    raise
                cases = []
            for case in cases:
                wave = case.get("wave")
                if not case.get("open"):
                    closed.add(wave)
                    continue
                if case.get("seconds_left") is not None:
                    caps[wave] = time.time() + case["seconds_left"]
                if case["case_id"] not in started and case.get("seconds_left"):
                    if wave not in {c.get("wave") for c in cases if c["case_id"] in started}:
                        recorder.event(
                            "wave_started",
                            wave=wave,
                            theme=case.get("theme"),
                            seconds_left=case.get("seconds_left"),
                        )
                        log.warning("wave %s started: %s", wave, case.get("theme"))
                    started[case["case_id"]] = pool.submit(
                        play_case,
                        client,
                        recorder,
                        case["case_id"],
                        new_strategy,
                        data,
                        case=case,
                        deadline=lambda w=wave: caps.get(w),
                    )
            time.sleep(poll)
    out = []
    for case_id, future in started.items():
        try:
            out.append(future.result())
        except Exception as e:
            out.append({"case_id": case_id, "error": repr(e)})
    return out

                method,
                path,
                endpoint,
                response if error is None else None,
                elapsed,
                attempt,
                move_id,
                waited,
                error,
                context,
            )
            if error is not None:
                if attempt == self.retries:
                    raise ArenaError(0, error, method, path)
                time.sleep(0.5 * 2**attempt)
                continue
            retry_after = response.headers.get("Retry-After", "")
            short = retry_after.isdigit() and int(retry_after) <= MAX_RETRY_AFTER_S
            retryable = response.status_code in RETRY_STATUS and not (response.status_code == 429 and not short)
            if not retryable or attempt == self.retries:
                break
            if self.recorder:
                self.recorder.metrics.incr("http.retry")
            time.sleep(float(retry_after) if retry_after.isdigit() else 0.5 * 2**attempt)

  **Checks I ran:**
  - `uv run pytest -q`: 282 passed, 8 xfailed, in 90 s.
  - `negotiator sim bench tactical --opponents all --jitter --strangers --reps 3`: 8 recorded cases × 3 reps × 6 opponent types.

  | walker | 0.63 | 0.00 | 96% |
  | deadline | 0.76 | 0.41 | 100% |
  | manipulator | 0.56 | 0.00 | 92% |
  
  - **Every 0 and every no-deal in the bench is case:P11 (quality_first):** hardball s0–s2, walker s2, manipulator s0 and s2.
  - **Why:** the opening breaks the ppm must-have, so C_open is the cheaper non-compliant opening. The supplier's compliant final offer (52.9, C 876k) stays above C_open (818k), the guard refuses it and the agent walks away.
  - The alternative is also above C_open, so it scores 0 either way. These opponents are invented, so read this as a stress test only.
  - `--json` printed a table, not JSON; the results are taken from `agent/runs-sim/20261011-0259*/summary.json`.
  
  ### 1. Levers and features missing from the 10 hosted practice cases
  All 19 case files are in `agent/runs/prod-traces/cases.json`.
  
  **Type/goal pairs played on the arena:**
  - price_increase/stabilise (P01, P02)
  - renewal/stabilise (P03)
  - renewal/routine (P04)
  - rfq/leverage (P05)
  - bundling/routine (P07)
  - raw_material/leverage (P08, P18)
  - capacity/secure_supply (P10)
  - quality/quality_first (P11)
  
  Every hosted type/goal pair rests on one case, except raw_material/leverage (P08 and P18, the same index AS-14404).
  
  **In case files only, never played on the arena:**
  - rfq/stabilise with negotiable tooling (P06, 2 suppliers, no own-plant should-cost for either)
  - capacity with a payment lever and a lead-time must-have (P09)
  - quality with lead time (P12)
  - price_increase/leverage with effective_date (P13)
  - renewal/stabilise with an index clause (P14)
  - a 3-part bundle (P15)
  - raw material on PPI-C241 (P16)
  - price_increase/stabilise with volume (P17)
  
  **In no case at all:**
  - a negotiable incoterm
  - must-haves on payment, contract, incoterm, index or chargeback, or on ppm outside quality cases; the `==` and `!=` operators
  - round_limit other than 10
  - a multi-part RFQ
  - quality_first on any type other than quality; leverage on bundling, renewal or capacity; secure_supply outside capacity
  - a stabilise bundle
  - case `facts`
  - the Sunday release
  
  **How tactical copes:**
  - Option fields go through a generic menu (`menu.combos`/`priced_menu`, menu.py:52-113) and C-optimisation (`baseline._optimise`, baseline.py:285). So incoterm, tooling and effective_date work with no special code, and deadband 5 is chosen by C, not hard-coded.
  - The only lever-specific code: `_trade_terms` (tactical.py:1195) covers only payment, contract and volume, and it is dead code (never called).
  - `TRADE_WORDS` (tactical.py:1488) has no `tooling_eur` entry: cosmetic.
  - An unknown goal falls back to the `routine` policy (tactical.py:73).
  
  ### 2. Ranked risks for unseen cases (impact × likelihood)
  
  **1. HIGH – a stabilise or secure_supply case without the supplier's own-plant should-cost (or a bundle).**
  - **Where:**
    - `_full_cost` returns None (tactical.py:344-355).
    - So `_estimate_supplier` drops the margin charge from our C (tactical.py:381-383).
    - With no estimate, the `RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR` guard is skipped (tactical.py:1092).
  - **What happens:**
    - groundtruth gives a floor of quote×0.99 (single-supplier price talks) or ×0.86 (RFQ) (groundtruth.py:189-192).
    - Once the supplier drops below it, `_reanchor` asks 10% under its price (tactical.py:901-919), with no goal check.
    - In an RFQ, rival quotes push it further.
  - **Exposure:**
    - Only 18 of the 46 contract suppliers have an own-plant should-cost.
    - P06 (stabilise RFQ) is exactly this case.
    - The charge at a 0-margin deal reaches 8% of spend (P03: 312k on 3.8M; P10: 210k). That is about the whole room, so the score becomes 0, as on P02 at 345.39.
  - **Fix:** when the goal is in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS and there is no own should-cost:
    - estimate full cost from `groundtruth.full_cost` (the generic DE should-cost × country);
    - else use the cheapest opening × (1 − sustainable_margin/100) × 0.98;
    - skip `_reanchor` for these goals when no estimate exists.
  
  **2. MED-HIGH – the 8-minute wave cap.**
  - **Where:**
    - runner.py:23: `CLOSE_BEFORE_DEADLINE_S=90`.
    - tactical.py:519: decide holds below 120 s.
    - The `with ThreadPoolExecutor` exit waits for in-flight sends (runner.py:96-125).
  - **Why:**
    - Practice replies were measured up to 83 s (p95 about 70 s).
    - The arena serves one session's calls one after another (runner.py:20 comment).
    - In a 2–3 supplier RFQ, a send started at T−121 s can delay `conclude` past the cap: `wave_cap`, no deal.
  - **Never tested:** practice sessions ran without a deadline and took 30–144 s.
  - **Fix:**
    - No new send when seconds left < 90 + (live threads × the slowest reply seen).
    - On close, use `pool.shutdown(wait=False)` and accept at once.
    - Rehearse on sandbox with an artificial deadline of about 240 s.
  
  **3. MED – a held thread with ≤2 rounds left gets no keepalive (tactical.py:1446-1447).**
  - If it is waiting on a rival (`_take_agreed` 856-860, or "last word: take it"), it times out.
  - One timeout after the last round ends the thread, and the agreed or final offer is lost.
  - **Fix:** in the coordinator (runner.py:112-123), when a held thread has no keepalive and its reply is about 40 s old, call `conclude` right away.
  
  **4. MED – constants tuned on one or two cases, applied to every case.**
  
  | Constant | Where | Tuned on | Risk on an unseen case |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `ANCHOR_ROUTINE` 0.13 | tactical.py:87, 454-457 | P07 only (P-25) | Every routine case gets 13%, including routine RFQ or raw material, where 25% would be right. |
  | `ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS` 0.25 + `ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA` 0.05 | tactical.py:76-77 | — | Applies to leverage, quality_first and unknown goals. |
  | `Policy.anchor`, `MAX_ANCHOR_LEVERAGE`, `GUESS_ANCHOR` | tactical.py:62-93, 307-327 | — | Dead code: the underutilised / full_order_book / price_frozen traits never change the first ask, although the comment at :90 says deeper asks lost credibility at P05. |
  | `ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY` 0.10, `STOP_ROOM` / `UPPER_ROOM_SHARE` | :88, :118 | P01 | |
  | `SHOULD_COST_SHARE` 0.98 | :81 | P01–P03 charges | If a supplier's real cost is above 0.98×should-cost, a deal can score 0. |
  | `CASH_SHORT_RATE` 1.2 | :84 | P01 | The belief uses ×2 at :257 – inconsistent. |
  | `RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR` 0.95 | :85 | P02 | |
  | `RELATIONSHIP_STEP` 0.25 / `RELATIONSHIP_MIN_STEP` 0.05 | :120-121, 692-698 | P01, P02, D01 | |
  | `REANCHOR` 0.10 | :113 | D01, D02 | |
  | `FLOOR_PRICE_ONLY` 0.99 / `FLOOR_WITH_LEVERS` 0.86 | groundtruth.py:32-34 | leave-one-out over the practice C_best | Unseen combinations take the nearest bucket. For leverage price_increase (P13 type) lower_c sits almost at the quote, so `_reanchor` fires after the first drop above 1%. |
  | Reply regexes (ROOM, FIRM, APPROVAL, MUST_CLAUSE, REQUESTS) | tactical.py:96-131, menu.py:19-45 | practice bot wording | New personas may word "final" differently. The `final_offer` status still catches the formal case. |
  
  - **Minimal general fix:** make floors and anchors depend on the goal and the levers present, not the case type. Re-enable `policy.anchor` or delete it so it does not mislead.
  
  **5. LOW-MED – must-have fields we cannot read mean every accept is refused (guards.py:28-34, 51-52).**
  - The quote PDFs of P01, P02, P03 and P10 name neither payment terms nor Incoterm.
  - A must-have on a field that is neither negotiable nor fixed (ppm or chargeback outside a quality case) means walking away.
  - **Fix:** fall back to the supplier master data, as `_standard_terms` already does (tactical.py:357-377).
  
  **6. LOW – the 8 xfails (4 variants × data/nodata):**
  
  | Variant | What happens | Could it happen in the final? |
  |---|---|---|
  | (a) must-have on a negotiable field without term_options | The agent holds; no deal. | Unlikely: api.md says negotiable fields take option values. |
  | (b) unknown negotiable field without options | The sheet goes out with None, gets a 422, the thread is held; the opening is refused, so the case scores the alternative. | Unlikely: "no new rules". |
  | (c) unit_price in `fixed_terms` | Cost is inf; we hold, then walk away; score 0. | Unlikely. |
  | (d) round_limit 1 | We hold on the last round and never send an offer (tactical.py:516-518). | Plausible: "default 10" implies other values. Fix: allow the last message when no offer has been sent yet. |
  
  - The null-parts and null-round_limit crashes are fixed (tactical.py:238, :516).
  
  **7. LOW – compute blow-up.**
  - I timed a P02 variant with more options (charge estimate on), first decide:
  
  | combos | first decide |
  |---|---|
  | 20 | 0.2 s |
  | 300 | 2.1 s |
  | 2700 | 16.5 s |
  
  - Practice cases have at most 60 combos.
  - A wave runs every case as threads in one process (GIL), so several large cases at once could pass 60 s per message.
  - **Fix:** prune the menu, or give each move a time budget.
  
  **8. LOW – fact leakage between cases.**
  - `WorldData.with_case` merges case facts into the shared object (data.py:82-86, called from session.py:140).
  - Parallel cases in a wave share it, so the ref guard accepts another case's IDs, which come back `contradicted`.
  - **Fix:** a per-case copy of `facts`.
  
  **9. OPERATIONAL, high impact – the Sunday release is not downloaded.**
  - `agent/data/release-sunday` does not exist yet.
  - WorldData is built once at startup (cli.py:64).
  - After 08:00: run `negotiator data`, restart the agent, and check that the release rows load before the final.
  
  **10. LOW – rival argument by unit price only** (baseline.py:365-385). It ignores whether the rival is dearer in C or breaks a must-have.
  
  The timing script is at `/Users/mikhail.fadin/.claude/jobs/16e44bb6/tmp/robust/t2.py`; the test and bench output is in `/Users/mikhail.fadin/.claude/jobs/16e44bb6/tmp/pytest.txt` and `bench.json`.

Scratch scripts are in `/Users/mikhail.fadin/.claude/jobs/16e44bb6/tmp/` (`summ.py`, `dec.py`, `p02.py`, `pts.py`, `show.py`).
  
  The main finding is about **when the supplier calls a final offer**. In P02, P07 and P08, all of the remaining gap is in the price or in the structure; none is in volume, freight or lead time.
  
  ## Cross-case mechanisms
  
  **G1. Supplier patience follows fresh verified arguments.** Sample: all cases except P05, supplier replies in round 2 or later where our best ask was at least 5% under its standing price.
  
  | What our message carried | Final offer | Mean drop | Held its price |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | A verified argument (n=109) | 4-7% | 1.3% | 9% |
  | No argument (n=163) | 53% | 1.06% | 58% |
  | Only a duplicate (n=16) | 94% | – | – |
  
  - Split by round:
    - Round 2: no argument 19% final, verified 3%, duplicate-only 93% (13 of 14 are P07).
    - Round 3: no argument 84% final (n=61, 23 of them P08), verified 6% (n=32).
  - Caveat: arguments that came back "does not change our calculation" also keep the supplier open (7% final), but 18 of those 27 replies are P11.
  
  **G2. The arena counts one argument per kind per case, not per ID, for forecasts too.** In bundle P07, `fc:360011`, `fc:360012` and `fc:360030` after `fc:360010` all came back `duplicate`.
  - `tactical._claims` dedupes across rounds only by ref (`src/negotiator/strategy/tactical.py:1250`), so it keeps citing a duplicate every round.
  - `data.evidence_orders` returns nothing for multi-part cases (`src/negotiator/data.py`, `len(part_ids) != 1`). P07 therefore has no order-line arguments, although `api.md` counts the orders of each part as a separate argument.
  
  **G3. Identical messages get different replies.** P08's first e-mail in `6a3708b9` and in `5f8dc86e`/`60790edb` is byte-identical. The first reply was 5.41 in one and 5.46 in the other, so a single P08 test carries about ±0.05 score of noise.
  
  **G4. Our ledger only uses falling windows that end at the series' latest month** (`ledger.recent_drop`). The arena accepts any window of at most 12 months that ends within the last 12 months. Falls that are valid but never cited:
  - P02: CU-NOTATION −2.2% (`idx:CU-NOTATION@2026-01` → `@2026-03`) and PPI-C241 −2.3% (2025-06 → 2025-11).
  - P08: LCI-C −0.26% (`idx:LCI-C@2025-10` → `@2026-01`). Only LCI-C rises were ever cited.
  
  **G5. "Which volume can you commit to?" is never answered with a number in the fixed-volume cases.** The suppliers ask it 42 times in P07, 34 in P08, 29 in P02 and 13 in P10.
  - The code to answer it (`_volume_answer`, `a6ec26c`) has run once, on P11. That supplier replied "we need some hard data or a binding order to really count on it" and moved nothing, so the evidence is weak.
  
  ## Per case
  
  ### P08 (raw material, leverage)
  - **Where it is lost.** Range 175,578, so 0.01 of score is EUR 1,756.
    - Our best is 5.28 with a 0 % deadband, 90 days, 24 months: C 1,025,948, which is 65.6k above C_best. The parts are the price (1,001,088), the index clause (27,029 plus index risk 4,505) and payment (−6,674).
    - House (0.75) needs 5.165 at deadband 0 or 5.285 at deadband 5 (−21.7k). Best (0.91) is about 5.14 at deadband 5.
    - Deadband 5 instead of 0 at the same price would be worth +0.128, but TRYED shows the supplier charges about the same for it, so the gap is in the price level.
  - **What moves it.**
    - The first reply sets the price: 5.41 when PPI-C2431's fall, AS-14404's fall and the order history open the talks.
    - After that the supplier gives −0.09 for the forecast, then −0.04, and calls its offer final in round 3. In every session round 3 carried no new argument.
    - AS falls get "not our reality" (hedged until March 2027). The owner's offer to walk us through his calculation (`doc:20260421-70710-M2`) was taken up in `7be3aab5`, and no breakdown followed.
  - **H-P08a (not in TRYED).** Keep a verified argument for rounds 3 and 4. Round 1: PPI-C2431 fall plus orders. Round 2: forecast. Round 3: AS-14404 fall (verified even when rejected) or LCI-C's −0.26% window (new series, not a duplicate).
    - It extends the TRYED row "one fresh citable argument per round" (unknown, P11/P01) to P08. `more_drops` failed because it reused a series; this does not.
    - Smallest test: 1-2 P08 practice sessions; judge against 0.626 with the ±0.05 noise from G3.
  
  ### P02 (copper, stabilise)
  - **Where it is lost.** Range 47,353, so 0.01 is EUR 474.
    - Our best is 362.02 with deadband 5 at 90 days: C 2,248,174. Its parts are a relationship charge of 32,091, index risk of 17,696 (0.8% of spend for any clause), payment −14,746 and quality 1,191.
  - **The clause structure has a ceiling.** I fitted the supplier's estimate exactly on all 36 recorded P02 deals: interest rate 0.066, full cost 367.6, standard payment 30 days. The best any clause can reach is 0.735, at 361.35 / deadband 5 / 90 days; we are already at 0.733.
    - The house's "0.74" is probably this ceiling rounded.
    - Best (0.85) and anything above 0.735 need a deal with **no clause** at 90 days: 369.6 gives about 0.74, 368.2 gives 0.85, 366 gives 0.99.
  - **Payment.** The supplier prices payment at about 6.2-6.6% a year against our 8%, so 90 days stays right.
  - **Where the no-clause path stopped.** It reached 373.88 → 373.22 → 372.62 (steps of about 0.6 a reply).
    - In `e11991f5` our asks stayed within about 1% of its price, and we accepted at round 3 of 10 while the supplier was still open.
    - In `37bdd1dc` we asked about 4% under. That sent a request to its pricing committee, and the supplier called 372.96 final.
    - TRYED's "stops at 372.62-372.96 whatever we ask" therefore rests on one session where we stopped ourselves.
  - **H-P02a (re-test of a failed TRYED row, with this new reading).** No clause, 90 days, asks within about 1-1.5% of its price. Never accept while it is open and above 369.6. Keep the deadband-5 sheet at 361.35 on the menu so the floor stays about 0.733. Test: 1 P02 session.
  - **H-P02b (new).** Add the older valid copper and PPI-C241 falls from G4 to that no-clause path. Test: offline check that the IDs are in `facts.json` (done), then combine with H-P02a in the same session.
  
  ### P07 (bundling, routine)
  - **Where it is lost.** Range 91,786, so 0.01 is EUR 918. All of it is in the price: 5.42 at 90 days / 24 months, C 323,061. House needs 5.36 (−3.6k) and best needs 5.31.
  - **Best against worst.**
    - 0.740: first ask 13% under, then within 4% from round 2. The supplier kept stepping −0.11, −0.03, −0.03 and called its offer final in round 4.
    - 0.663 cluster (9 sessions): first ask 26% under, then a duplicate forecast at an 18% gap, which brought a final offer in round 2.
    - 36 months costs us nothing over the 2-year horizon, but the supplier prices it the same as 24 after round 1.
  - **Supplier notes.** It has idle capacity ("second shift on hold"), and price changes above 2% need committee approval. P07's back office shows no committee notes, so that limit never came into play.
  - **H-P07a (new).** Dedupe arguments by kind across rounds (G2), and add order-line arguments per part for bundles. These are the supplier's own orders for 360010, 360012 and 360030, three separate arguments. Use them in rounds 2-4 instead of duplicate forecasts.
    - Smallest test: unit test that tactical never sends a second `fc:` once one is verified, then 1 P07 session.
  
  ### P10 (capacity, secure_supply)
  - **Where it is lost.** Range 603,565, so 0.01 is EUR 6,036.
    - Best is 31.5 at lead time 56, 24 months: C 1,522,963. Its parts are price 1,474,200, late delivery 33,600, payment 9,828 and quality 5,335. There is no relationship charge (should-cost 24.31).
    - House (0.69) is only about 7k away: 31.35 at lead time 56, or about 32.05 at 42. C_best is unreachable, since no team is above 0.70, so this is a ceiling.
  - **What works.**
    - Lead time 56 gets 1.9 off per unit and costs us 0.72 per unit.
    - A first ask about 4% under keeps round 1 open (33.6, alternative 31.7 at 54 days). Asks 15% or more under bring a final offer in round 1 (33.8, alternative 31.9).
    - Round 2 is always final. The one round-2 ask under its alternative (31.27 against 31.7) got 31.5, the midpoint.
  - **H-P10a (new, one observation).** In round 2, ask about 3% under its alternative on the alternative's structure (lead time 56), expecting a midpoint near 31.2-31.3.
    - TRYED's "ask beyond the band" row is about the committee, not this. TRYED's "accept the alternative by its ID" (unknown) is worth only about +0.008.
    - Test: 1 P10 session.
  
  ## Scoring nuance
  P02's and P10's gaps to the house (0.002 and 0.011) are within the board's two-decimal rounding of the house score. The real below-house gaps are P08 (0.124) and P07 (0.04).

content.text:
# Review: where the score is, and what to do next

I didn't change any files or spend any practice quota. Everything below comes from code review, the 293 recorded sessions, and the cost function run offline. I re-checked the most important findings in the code myself.

## How the work has been done
- **Good:** our cost estimate matches the arena's cost exactly on every recorded deal. Tried ideas are written down, and new ideas sit behind flags so they can be switched on one at a time.
- **Weak spot 1, noise:** two byte-identical first e-mails on P08 got different first replies (5.41 and 5.46). That is about ±0.05 of score. The gameplan's rule "bots are deterministic, one session per change" doesn't hold. Several ideas were dropped on a −0.02 single-session difference, which is inside this noise (e.g. `more_drops`, `band_steps` on P08).
- **Weak spot 2, overfitting:** most constants were tuned on one practice case. Examples: the 13 % first ask for `routine` (P07 only) and the 4 % first ask for strategic suppliers (that one also cost D01 0.969 → 0.749). The final plays **hidden cases**. So a fix that makes the agent robust is worth more than tuning P08 further.
- **Weak spot 3, the final itself:** the code that runs the final has paths that can lose whole cases or waves. It has never been rehearsed against a deadline.

## Directions, by value and safety

### A. Fixes that protect the final (do these first; free to test)
1. **One polling error ends the whole final.** `runner.py:197-201` re-raises any error except 403 from the case-list poll. A single 5xx or network failure stops the loop, and no later wave is started. Fix: catch it, log it, sleep, poll again.
2. **A case that fails to open is never retried.** `runner.py:219` marks a case as started before its session opens. If opening fails (a 429, which has no `Retry-After` here, or a 5xx), that case scores nothing. Fix: retry with backoff while the wave is open, and only mark it started once the session is open.
3. **A strategic goal without the supplier's own-plant cost estimate can score 0.** `tactical.py:344-383`: in a `stabilise` or `secure_supply` case where we have no should-cost for that supplier's own plant, the relationship charge drops out of our cost estimate. `_reanchor` (`tactical.py:901`) then asks 10 % under the supplier's price. That is the same pattern that scored P02 zero at 345.39. Only 18 of 46 suppliers have such an estimate, and unplayed case P06 is exactly this shape. Fix: fall back to a generic cost estimate, and don't re-anchor on these goals when no estimate exists.
4. **Closing can run past the 8-minute wave cap.** E-mails already being sent and keepalives can delay the accept past the cap, and the case then counts as no deal. Fix: no new sends after a closing flag is set, accept without waiting for the worker pool, and rehearse on sandbox with an artificial deadline of about 240 s.
5. **Case facts leak between parallel cases.** `data.py:82-86` `with_case` writes each case's facts into one shared object. Cases running in parallel in a wave can then cite another case's IDs, which come back `contradicted`. Fix: a copy per case.
6. **Merge `fix/timeout-moves`.** Its conflicts are trivial and the tests pass after merging (103 passed). It fixes offers lost after a timeout on multi-supplier cases: P05 had 24 timeouts over 9 sessions, and those sessions scored 0.27–0.71 against 0.74–0.82 without.
7. **Smaller items:**
   - `round_limit=1` means we never send an offer (one of the 8 known test failures).
   - A must-have on a field we can't read means every accept is refused; fall back to the supplier's master data.
   - A held thread with ≤2 rounds left gets no keepalive and can time out, losing an agreed offer.

### B. General negotiation levers (practice runs needed to confirm)
1. **Never send a round without a fresh, verified argument.** Supplier replies in round 2 or later, by what our message carried:

   | What our message carried | Supplier answered with a final offer |
   |---|---|
   | A verified argument | 4–7 % |
   | No argument | 53 % |
   | Only a duplicate argument | 94 % |

   - The arena counts one argument per *kind* per case, not per ID. Our dedupe works per ID, so we keep re-sending duplicates (P07's forecasts).
   - Fix: dedupe by kind across rounds and hold a verified argument back for rounds 3–4.
   - Bundles currently get no order-history arguments: `data.py:302` skips multi-part cases, although each part's orders count separately.
2. **Falling index windows we never cite.** `ledger.recent_drop` only uses windows that end at the latest month. The arena accepts any window of up to 12 months that ends within the last year. Examples: on P02 a copper fall of −2.2 % and a PPI fall of −2.3 %; on P08 an LCI-C window of −0.26 %. This adds arguments without breaking any rule.
3. **Take a cheaper alternative sheet even when the saving is small.** `tactical.py:782` only takes the supplier's alternative if it saves 0.2 % of total cost. It should be a share of the negotiable room instead. Worth about +0.009 on P08; small, but safe.

### C. Case-specific, lower priority
- **P02:** any index clause caps the score at 0.735, and we're at 0.733. Going higher needs a deal without a clause at about 369 or less. The earlier "no-clause failed" verdict rests on a session where we stopped ourselves while the supplier was still moving.
- **P10:** at the house level (a 0.011 gap, inside the board's rounding); spend no attempts.
- **P07:** the real gap to the house is 0.04, all in price; argument dedupe (B1) is the lever.
- **P08:** the real gap to the house is 0.12. B1 and B2 apply.

## Suggested order before the freeze (gameplan: 10:30)
1. A1–A5 plus merge A6. Test with `make test`, a sandbox D01/D02 run, and a short-deadline rehearsal. None of this spends quota.
2. B1 and B2 as flags, checked on sandbox. Then practice P07 + P08 + P02. That's 3 sessions per repetition, and you need at least 2 repetitions because of the ±0.05 noise. That needs your explicit yes, with the balance from `negotiator me` first.
3. Operational: download the Sunday data release after 08:00 and restart the agent (data loads once at startup). Before the final, check `negotiator sessions` shows no open sessions and nobody else is playing on the key.

The scratch scripts and per-session tables are in `/Users/mikhail.fadin/.claude/jobs/16e44bb6/tmp/`. Should I implement the A-block on a branch?

# Ревью и план до финала, 11 октября 2026

Написано 11 октября 2026, около 03:30 CEST, на `main` `a0768a0`. Сессии практики не тратились. Источники: ревью
кода, 293 записанные сессии практики (`agent/data/replays/`, `agent/data/backoffice/`), прогоны в `agent/runs/`,
стоимость C пересчитана офлайн через `arena_kit.cost`. Скрипты и таблицы по сессиям лежат во временной папке
задачи, в репозиторий не вносились.

Здесь только найденное и план. Ожидаемых прибавок к score нет: их запишем после прогона, который их проверит.

## 1. Как сделана работа

**Хорошо:**
- наш C совпадает с C арены на каждой проверенной сделке, включая индексную оговорку и relationship charge;
- идеи ведутся в `TRYED.md`, изменения включаются флагами по одному.

  `5f8dc86e`/`60790edb`). Это около ±0.05 score. Правило из `gameplan-2026-10-11.md` «боты детерминированы,
  одной сессии хватает» не выполняется. Часть идей отброшена по разнице −0.02 в одной сессии, а это внутри шума
  (`more_drops`, `band_steps` на P08).
- **Переобучение.** Почти каждая константа подобрана на одном кейсе практики: первый запрос 13 % для `routine`
  (только P07), кэп 4 % на первый запрос для стратегических поставщиков (он же опустил D01 с 0.969 до 0.749,
  `runs.md` S-22), `SHOULD_COST_SHARE` 0.98, `RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR` 0.95. В финале будут **скрытые кейсы**, так
  что устойчивость важнее дальнейшей подгонки под P08.
- **Код самого финала** не прогоняли с дедлайном волны ни разу, и в нём есть пути, на которых теряется кейс или вся
  волна (раздел 2).
